summary: High-level security and business continuity review focused on incident response, RTO/RPO targets, escalation paths, and SLA uptime commitments. Equinox wants clarity on SOC 2/ISO artifacts, KMS/BYOK options, cross-region failover, and how Redwood's Dedicated and Private options support faster RTOs. Agreed to tabletop drill and exchange of runbooks; Redwood to provide artifacts and PagerDuty integration notes.
topics: KMS / BYOK / HSM and key custody
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-02 15:00 UTC | Duration 62m | Recording: FF auto | Agenda: IR + BCDR, SLA, Escalation

00:00:03 Alice (AE): hi everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run through service continuity, sla targets, and the escalation flow. I'm Alice from Redwood. ben, priya are with me.
00:00:12 Marcus (CTO): thanks, we just want to validate that during a region outage our RTOs are realistic and what access we'll have to logs and keys.
00:00:22 Ben (SE): yep, quick note - i'll call out that Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private are different from hosted. private gives you a separate control plane in your VPC, key custody patterns differ.
00:00:35 Karen (Head of Security): can you confirm SOC 2 Type II is current and how we can get evidence? we also need ISO 27001 scope.
00:00:44 Alice (AE): absolutely, we'll share the cert bundle. note there's a short ND A redaction process for some vendor-only evidence but the typical pack includes SOC 2 report, iso cert, pen test summary.
00:00:55 Dina (DR lead): for IR we are focused on three tiers: critical payment pipelines (RTO 15m), underwriting services (RTO 2h), analytics (RTO 24h). RPO targets: payment <5m, underwriting <30m, analytics daily. is that feasible?
00:01:14 Ben (SE): ok, practical bit - on hosted we rely on cross-region replication with async copies; RTOs for sub- minute are hard without Dedicated or private colocated replicas. Dedicated gives you pinned GPU pools and faster warm standby options which reduce RTO.
00:01:30 Karen: what about encryption keys? we need BYOK and HSM-backed keys; Equinox cannot have vendor-owned keys for PII.
00:01:39 Ben: we support BYOK via KMS integrations - you can bring keys via customer KMS or use Redwood-managed HSM with separation of duties. note the audit trail for key usage is available in the audit logs, though sometimes the auto transcription of the log names looks odd in exports.
00:01:56 Omar (Compliance): retention for logs? we need WORM storage for 7 years for some lines of business. can you do that?
00:02:04 Alice: yes, audit logs can be exported to your S3 with WORM / object lock. retention and export cadence configurable. we'll include the steps in the runbook.
00:02:12 Marcus: SLA conversation — we currently see 99.95 for a critical path. Equinox is sensitive to 4 9s for some corridors. what's realistic from Redwood?
00:02:23 Ben: hosted plan currently targets 99.9 for availability; Dedicated has higher SLO options and we offer enterprise SLA with credits for downtime. 99.99 is possible on Dedicated with cross-region active-passive and stricter ops calendar. we'll surface the math - it's about resource reservation and failover automation.
00:02:40 Speaker 1 (Legal observed): credits mechanism - how does that work for partial outages?
00:02:46 Alice: typically in the contract we define credit tiers, detection windows, and the customer files a claim with metrics. we'll share sample contract language.
00:02:55 Dina: escalation matrix — we want a clear war-room and point of contact. who will be on call from Redwood?
00:03:02 Priya (CS): we provide an escalation list: first-line support, then SE on-call, then an on-call engineering lead; for Dedicated you can get a named technical account owner and optional 24/7 pager coverage.
00:03:13 Karen: do you integrate with PagerDuty / OpsGenie?
00:03:16 Ben: yes, PD/OG integrations supported; we'll send the playbook, webhook examples and a sample runbook with the exact webhook paths. sometimes the webhook docs get truncated in the copy but we'll verify.
00:03:30 Marcus: for incident detection, do you provide anomaly alerts or just the logs?
00:03:35 Ben: Console has latency/cost traces, token-level breakdowns, and alerting hooks; you can route to PD for on-call triggers. we also have automated fallback policies that can reroute to a compatible model variant if capacity is degraded. note: fallback will change latencies and possibly cost.
00:03:58 Dina: tabletop drills — we want to run one with a region AWS outage and a key compromise scenario. can Redwood facilitate?
00:04:05 Alice: yes. propose 30-45 min tabletop where we simulate an outage, trigger the runbook, and validate escalation path. we'll also run a key-rotation BYOK scenario.
00:04:18 Omar: if keys are compromised, do you have HSM attestations and rotation steps?
00:04:23 Ben: HSM-backed keys support rotation; we keep a key-usage audit. if BYOK is used, you control the rotation and can revoke. we'll provide steps for key compromise containment and rotating tokens across services.
00:04:38 Karen: data residency — some workloads must remain in EU. does cross-region replication move data outside region?
00:04:45 Ben: you can configure replication policies by model route; for EU-only apps we keep replicas in eu-west regions only. if you require strict residency, Private deployment in your VPC ensures data plane never leaves your network.
00:04:59 Marcus: curious about RPO when switching to a replica — during failover will we lose ongoing KV cache state?
00:05:05 Ben: for generative workloads KV cache is ephemeral; for stateful services we snapshot and replicate at configurable intervals. RPO depends on snapshot cadence — for sub-5m RPO we'd use near- real-time replication which increases network/ingress load. we'll map costs.
00:05:20 Dina: can you show the escalation matrix now?
00:05:23 Alice: sure, quick overview — Level 1 (support), Level 2 (SE on-call), Level 3 (SRE/Engineering lead), Exec notif after 2hrs. PagerDuty escalation steps in doc.
00:05:33 Marcus: what's the exec notif SLA?
00:05:36 Priya: exec notif triggers for Sev1 after 30min of no mitigations, or after failover. details can be adjusted in the contract.
00:05:47 Omar: audit evidence — we need machine-readable logs for the last 13 months and a way to query them.
00:05:53 Ben: logs can be streamed to your S3 or BigQuery; search/export formats include JSON with timestamps. we'll include the sample query and retention config.
00:06:02 Karen: are there any known single points of failure in Redwood Dedicated?
00:06:07 Ben: architecture is zonal; for Dedicated we recommend multi-az or cross-region standbys. single-site Dedicated could be an SPOF for certain control-plane ops but data plane replication mitigates most user-visible outages.
00:06:20 Marcus: insurance compliance asks for RTO proof points; can you provide historical incident time-to-recover metrics?
00:06:28 Alice: we can provide anonymized runbook execution metrics and postmortem summaries redacted for customer names. will include as part of the evidence pack.
00:06:40 Dina: in a DR test how do we validate data integrity after failover?
00:06:45 Ben: suggested steps: checksum validation on snapshot, smoke tests for critical endpoints, token-level generation sanity checks. we'll provide a test checklist.
00:06:56 Marcus: maintenance windows — what is your policy on planned downtime vs emergency maintenance and SLA exclusions?
00:07:03 Priya: planned maintenance is notified 72h in advance, not counted against SLA if within window; emergency maintenance will be communicated ASAP and handled case-by-case. we'll include contract language in the sample SLA.
00:07:17 Karen: do you do runbook dry-runs? some vendors just hand over docs.
00:07:21 Alice: we run the drill with you, walk the steps, and can run an ops-play with your SREs. that's what the tabletop is for.
00:07:28 Marcus: are there any fees for running drills?
00:07:31 Alice: initial tabletop is complimentary during onboarding; full-scale DR tests may be scoped as professional services.
00:07:40 Omar: supply chain questions — do you have subcontractor lists and where are the backups stored?
00:07:46 Ben: we maintain a vendor annex and will share redacted list. backups are stored in customer-controlled buckets or encrypted vendor buckets with customer-controlled keys depending on deployment.
00:07:59 Dina: action item recap?
00:08:02 Alice: sure - we'll send SOC2/ISO pack, runbook PDF, PagerDuty integration doc, and a sample SLA excerpt. Dina will send RTO/RPO workload list. schedule tabletop week of Dec 15.
00:08:18 Marcus: sounds good. thanks all.
00:08:22 Karen: thanks.
